entries.msgstr: CLOSE

Crew directives provide a specific perk trained to 100% for a single battle if the crew does not already have it. If the crew already has the perk trained to 100% and its efficiency has not been reduced, directives enhance it. Retraining Orders allow you to reset a crew member's trained perks for free without losing XP.

If a crew member is not selected for a certain vehicle, they are located in the Barracks. The Barracks contain all crew members, including recruits. Recruits are new crew members without perks. You can configure them upon recruitment.
Go to the Appearance section of a crew member to change their name and appearance. There, you can also select unique crew skins for the crew member.
Additional Features
The crew is an essential part of any vehicle. The crew composition depends on the specific vehicle. A crew might comprise from 1 to 6 crew members.
Each qualification affects a certain element of vehicle efficiency.

Crew members have different qualifications: Commander, Gunner, Driver, Radio Operator, and Loader. Each qualification allows them to train special perks that will help them emerge victorious from the most challenging situations.
Vehicle Crew
Use First Aid Kits to treat injured crew members and remove the stun effect.
A crew can be stunned by SPG fire, which will temporarily decrease the combat performance of your vehicle.
A crew member can be injured in battle, which significantly reduces the performance of the vehicle in areas related to their qualification.
Injured Crew Members

If you fight a battle in an Elite vehicle with the Accelerate Crew Training option enabled, the crew earns more Crew XP. In this case, the Combat XP earned in this vehicle will be added to the least experienced crew member.
To train and improve a crew member's perks, Crew XP is needed. Your vehicle earns a certain amount of Combat XP in every battle you fight, while its crew members earn the same amount of Crew XP.
You can also convert Free XP into Crew XP (5 Crew XP for 1 Free XP), or study Crew Books to get more Crew XP.
Crew Experience
The Commander provides a bonus to the efficiency of all other crew members. Crew efficiency can also be increased using certain crew perks, or some equipment and consumables.
A crew efficiency bonus allows the crew's perks to be enhanced further, increasing the base characteristics of the vehicle they enter battle in.
The efficiency of each crew member influences the final combat parameters of a vehicle. The higher their efficiency, the higher the bonus.
Crew Efficiency

Bonus perks do not count toward the perk limit and do not require XP, and the number of bonus perks a crew member has depends on their number of major qualification perks. For every two trained major qualification perks, you receive one bonus perk for every additional qualification.
When one crew member has several qualifications, they will have bonus perks for each qualification—but this also means that an injury to them will have a more serious impact.

If a vehicle has several crew members with the same qualification, the effects of their perks are calculated as an average from all of them. This means if you want your perk to work at 100%, you have to train it to 100% for all crew members with the same qualification.
Additional Qualifications

The more experienced a crew member is, the more perks they can train, up to a maximum of 6 perks in their major qualification. Each qualification has a set of its unique perks and 3 Group Perks available to all crew members.

The more a perk has been trained, the stronger its effect. There is also a general Perk Efficiency parameter that influences the effect of all a crew member's perks. Initially, it is set at 100%, but it can be reduced while retraining for another vehicle.

Perks are trained one after the other, and training each subsequent perk requires twice as much XP as the last. Some crew members may have a "zero" perk. Zero perks do not require XP for training, meaning subsequent perks can be trained faster.
Crew Perks

To use their perks in battle in a specific vehicle, a crew member must be trained to operate that vehicle. Premium and reward vehicles are an exception: if a crew member is trained to operate a vehicle of a certain type, they can operate all Premium and reward vehicles of that type using their perks without additional training.

If a crew member's perk efficiency was reduced as a result of retraining, all their earned XP will go toward increasing it. Once their perk efficiency is back at 100%, the XP they earn will again go toward training new perks.

To train a crew member for a specific vehicle, the appropriate specialization and type of retraining must be selected. After this, the previous specialization will be replaced with the new one. However, some types of retraining may reduce the crew member's perk efficiency.
Specialization

The Commander keeps track of the combat situation on the battlefield and commands the crew. Each Commander has a special feature — Sixth Sense. It allows the Commander to determine whether the vehicle has been spotted.
The Driver handles the vehicle mobility and aims to decrease gun dispersion on the move. The Radio Operator reports enemy positions, allowing your team to cooperate on the battlefield.
The Gunner is responsible for shot accuracy and targeting vulnerable areas. The Loader is responsible for preparing shells and reloading speed. Together, they provide your firepower.
